findings.title: The new foreign key makes a vet with visits undeletable — DELETE /api/vets/{id} returns 500
findings.body: vet_id gets no ON DELETE clause and nothing on the JPA side nulls it out, so delete(vet) raises a foreign-key violation the advice turns into a 500. Verified live this run: DELETE /api/vets/4 → HTTP 500, violates foreign key constraint "visits_vet_id_fkey". The backfill gives every seeded vet a visit, so on a fresh database none of the six can be deleted.
findings.why: Three defensible answers: ON DELETE SET NULL, a guard in deleteVet answering 409, or “a vet who has attended is not deletable”. Returning 500 is not one of them.

snippets.caption: No ON DELETE clause on the new constraint.
And nothing between the request and the violation.

findings.title: The V9 backfill hardcodes vet ids 1–6, and the comment above it is not true of every database
findings.body: The UPDATE assumes the six V3-seeded vets still occupy ids 1–6. DELETE /api/vets/{id} is exposed, so in any long-lived database where a seeded vet was removed this violates visits_vet_id_fkey: Flyway aborts and the app does not start.
findings.why: Also false wherever a visit was booked through the UI. Selecting from the vets that actually exist costs one subquery and removes both problems.

snippets.caption: Both the claim and the arithmetic that depends on it.

findings.title: The vet dropdown calls a VET_ADMIN endpoint from two OWNER_ADMIN screens, and the 403 is swallowed
findings.body: The 403 is swallowed into an empty array, so the select renders with nothing but -- not assigned -- and no error.
findings.why: Masked today: petclinic.security.enable is false by default and the one seeded user holds all three roles, so no test catches it. PetTypeRestController sets the precedent — hasAnyRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN, @roles.VET_ADMIN) — but widening an authorization rule is a contract decision.

snippets.caption: The role the whole controller requires.
…and where the 403 becomes an empty list.

findings.title: @ManyToOne Vet is EAGER, and only one of the four read paths join-fetches it
findings.body: The other three — GET /api/owners/{ownerId} (which the new e2e exercises), GET /api/visits/{visitId} and PetClinicMcp.listVisits — issue one select … from vets where id=? per visit. On the MCP tool that is N+1 across the whole clinic.
findings.why: LAZY trades a query count for a LazyInitializationException on any path that maps outside the transaction. That trade is yours.

snippets.caption: EAGER by omission — @ManyToOne defaults to it.
The one query that was taught about the vet.

findings.title: An unknown vetId answers 404, for a resource the client is trying to create
findings.body: orElseThrow() throws NoSuchElementException, which the advice maps to 404 with a bare "Not found!" string body rather than the ProblemDetail every other handler returns. POST /api/visits {"vetId": 9999} answers 404 and the client cannot tell a bad field from a bad URL.
findings.why: Its Javadoc says “an unknown one is rejected”; a 400 naming the field would match that intent. Left alone because a status code is a contract.

snippets.caption: The rule, and the throw that decides the status code.

findings.title: The map now says a visit has exactly one vet, and the code says it may have none
findings.body: DomainModelExtractor reads the model by plain reflection and ignores JPA annotations on purpose, so it can only mark a * end — an unmarked end reads as exactly one.
findings.why: Optionality is the central design decision of this change and the one thing the living diagrams cannot show; no test will complain either — the extractor that feeds them cannot see it.

snippets.caption: The Javadoc says 0..1; the diagram says 1.

findings.title: The deny that protects the generated openapi.yaml covers only one tool
findings.body: Edit(./openapi.yaml) blocks Edit and not Write, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit; the shell-write denies added earlier were dropped again. CLAUDE.md says hand-editing the file is denied, so the rule and the documentation disagree.
findings.why: Raised, not fixed, on purpose: an agent should not widen its own permission configuration because a review suggested it — and the ./ prefix in that glob is worth confirming actually matches first.

snippets.caption: The deny, and the three verbs it does not name.

findings.title: The sequence deltas carry rendering noise
findings.body: This branch moved the diagram generator itself — trace-to-puml.ts alone changed 102 lines — so the committed base diagrams were rendered by the old generator and arrows that never changed still read as removed-and-re-added: 45 of 54 arrows red in add-visit, 34 of 64 in owner-search, a scenario this feature does not touch at all.
findings.why: Red means “rendered differently”, not “changed”. In add-visit, the listVets / GET /api/vets arrows are genuinely new. Re-recording the base side with the base generator needs the stack running on the base commit, and its ports are fixed.

findings.title: Which line should a diagram header point at — the comment, or the declaration?
findings.body: The existing test pins the opposite rule on purpose, at line 3 of its fixture: a comment naming the test is still where a reviewer wants to land. The applied fix was reverted; the file is untouched by this branch.
findings.why: Which rule you actually want is a call for whoever reads these diagrams.

snippets.caption: The preference the revert put back.

sections.title: Where the design system was not used
sections.body:
main introduced app-combo — one standardised single-select that marks its host data-ds="combo" — and moved every existing single-select onto it. This branch adds a vet picker to two screens and puts only one of them on the component.

Flagged: a native control filling a role the design system covers, with no [data-ds] above it. The roles are derived from the components themselves — the attribute is the registry — so controls the design system has no component for, like the multi-select on Edit a vet, are listed as considered and deliberately not judged.

Nothing else in the repository catches this. Not ESLint, not the guardrails, not Cucumber: app-combo renders an inner <select> carrying the same id, so page.locator('select#vetId') in add-visit.spec.ts matches either implementation identically.

sections.title: One opt-in, three test languages, four diagrams
sections.body:
Every diagram in this tab was drawn from real OpenTelemetry traces of a test run, and every test that produced one opts in the same way: @generate_sequence as a Cucumber scenario tag in a .feature, the identical string as a Playwright tag in a .spec.ts, and @GenerateSequence on a @SpringBootTest in Java. Nothing else about a test changes in order to be drawn.

The Java pair is the cheapest of the three to record. AddVisitSequenceTest is an in-memory integration test — no Chromium, no Angular, no running server, an embedded Postgres thrown away with the JVM — and it still exercises the real controller, the real transaction boundaries and the real Hibernate session, which is why its N+1 is the same N+1 the browser diagrams show. The JVM writes the very same trace-window file the browser suites write, and the very same generator turns it into a .puml; nothing in the renderer had to learn what a @SpringBootTest is. What it does need is Tempo up (./start-grafana.sh) and the OpenTelemetry Java agent attached, which is what petclinic-backend/run-tests-with-tracing.sh arranges. Under a plain mvn test the tracer is a no-op, the annotation costs nothing, and it is an ordinary test.

The generator itself moved on this branch, so arrows that never changed still read as removed-and-re-added. The last finding on the Review tab measures how much.

note: A visit now records the vet that attended it — merge-base 5acf2472.

assumptions.title: The attending vet is optional at every layer — a visit nobody attended is a legal, permanent state
assumptions.body: Issue #37 asks that a visit “be linked to the vet that attended that consultation” and never says whether that link is mandatory. Six minutes in, the coder settled it as nullable everywhere — column, entity, both DTOs, no validation — and made -- not assigned -- the picker's first option. Nothing in the stack can now refuse a vet-less visit. “one design decision matters: vet should be optional/nullable since legacy rows and MCP-booked visits won't have one yet” — its own thinking, 13 Aug 23:00.
assumptions.alternative: Required on every new visit — @NotNull on VisitFieldsDto, NOT NULL after the backfill — with vet-less tolerated only for rows that predate the column.
assumptions.why: Whether a receptionist may save a visit naming no vet, and whether that is a legitimate resting state or a to-do something should chase.

snippets.caption: description carries @NotNull; vetId, right beneath it, carries only @Min(0).
Booking with nobody attending is the dropdown's first option.

assumptions.title: A PUT that omits vetId silently unassigns the attending vet
assumptions.body: updateVisit assigns resolveVet(visitDto.getVetId()) unconditionally, and vetId is a plain Integer — so “field absent” and “explicitly null” are the same wire value. Any client still sending the pre-feature body wipes the vet on every save. “I'm adding a helper method that resolves a vet by id, returning null if the id is null and throwing otherwise, then using it in both bookVisit and updateVisit” — its own thinking, 13 Aug 23:02. The two paths were never separated after that.
assumptions.alternative: Leave the recorded vet untouched when vetId is absent, and require an explicit null to unassign.
assumptions.why: Whether an older integration, or a partial form post, is allowed to erase attribution as a side effect. No test clears a vet, so nothing pins today's answer either.

snippets.caption: setVet runs on every update, with whatever the body did or did not carry.

assumptions.title: The picker offers every vet — no specialty, no availability, no double-booking rule
assumptions.body: The form loads getVets() and lists the whole clinic, unfiltered and unordered. The domain already models vet_specialties, and a visit already carries a date and an exact time, so narrowing by specialty or by who is free at that slot was available and was never weighed. Nothing prevents booking one vet for two visits at the same minute. “adding a vets array to visit-add, loading it in ngOnInit, and binding a select dropdown to vetId using ngValue” — its own thinking, 13 Aug 23:03, straight from “add a dropdown” to binding it.
assumptions.alternative: Offer only vets whose specialty fits, or only those with no clashing visit at that date and time — and reject a clashing vetId server-side.
assumptions.why: Whether picking a vet is scheduling, with the constraints that implies, or only record-keeping about who was there.

snippets.caption: The whole vets feed: getVets(), no filter, no awareness of the date being booked.

assumptions.title: The chatbot can read the attending vet but can never set one
assumptions.body: “Display its vet everywhere throughout the app” was read as display-only for the MCP surface: list_visits gained a vet name, create_visit gained no vet parameter. Every visit an owner books through the assistant is therefore vet-less until somebody opens the web form. “This keeps things least disruptive and avoids breaking the MCP create_visit path, so I'll move on to checking the remaining files rather than asking for clarification” — its own thinking, 13 Aug 23:00. That constraint is also what forced the column to stay nullable, so this call and the first one are the same call.
assumptions.alternative: Give create_visit an optional vetId, so the chat booking path carries what the web form does.
assumptions.why: Whether owners booking by chat are meant to choose a vet at all, and who is expected to fill the gap on the visits they create.

snippets.caption: create_visit's four required parameters — pet, date, time, description; no vet.
